academic_translation:
If, like an actor, in another mode
That very thing is seen, it is not permanent.
If that other mode is that very thing,
That oneness is an unprecedented one.
translation: Someone might say it is like an actor playing a new part. But if that thing changes, it is not lasting forever. If that new part is the exact same thing, then this kind of oneness is completely unheard of.

academic_translation:
If that other mode is not true,
Then state its own nature.
If you say it is consciousness itself, then in that case,
It would follow that all persons are one.
translation: If that new part is not real, then tell me its own nature. If you say it is just awareness itself, then there is a problem. In that case, it would mean all people are exactly one person.

academic_translation:
The conscious and the non-conscious, too,
Would become one, because their existence is the same.
When specific differences are false,
What then is the basis for similarity?
translation: Things that can think and things that cannot think would also become one. This is because they both exist in the same way. When the differences between things are false, what makes them similar?

academic_translation:
That which is mindless is also not the self,
Because it is mindless, like a vase and so forth.
If, however, it cognizes because it is endowed with a mind,
It follows that the non-cognizer perishes.
translation: A thing without a mind is not the self. It is just like a vase. But you might say it knows things because it gets a mind. Then the thing that did not know anything before would be destroyed.

academic_translation:
But if there is no change in the self,
What has consciousness done to it?
Thus, lacking cognition and devoid of activity,
Space would be made into the self.
translation: If the self never changes, what does the mind actually do to it? An unchanging self cannot know or do anything. That would make space into the self.

academic_translation:
If you say: "If the self does not exist,
The connection between karma and result is illogical;
Because one perishes after performing a karma,
Whose karma will it be?"
translation: Someone might say: If the self does not exist, the link between action and result makes no sense. A person disappears after doing an action. So whose action will it be?

academic_translation:
That the action and the result have distinct bases,
And that the self has no activity therein,
Is established for both of us,
So is this debate here not pointless?
translation: We both agree that the action and the result happen to different things. We also agree that the self does nothing here. So is this argument not pointless?

academic_translation:
That the one possessing the cause is endowed with the result—
To see this is impossible.
It is by relying on a single continuum
That an agent and an experiencer are taught.
translation: It is impossible to see the exact same person holding the cause and the result. We talk about a doer and one who experiences only because they are part of a single continuing stream.

academic_translation:
The mind of the past and future
Is not the self, because it does not exist.
If, however, the arisen mind is the self,
When that perishes, there is no self either.
translation: A mind in the past or future is not the self, because it does not exist. But if the mind happening right now is the self, then when that mind disappears, there is no self either.

academic_translation:
Just as the trunk of a plantain tree
Is nothing when divided into parts,
Likewise, when sought through analysis,
The self is also not real.
translation: Think of a banana tree trunk. If you pull it apart piece by piece, nothing is left. It is the same when you look closely for a self. A real self cannot be found.

academic_translation:
"If sentient beings do not exist,
Toward whom should one practice compassion?"
Toward whatever is imputed by delusion,
Which is accepted for the sake of the result.
translation: Someone might ask, "If there are no living beings, who should we show compassion to?" We show compassion to those imagined by our confusion. We accept this confusion for the sake of the result.

academic_translation:
"If there are no sentient beings, whose is the result?"
That is true, yet it is asserted through delusion.
For the sake of pacifying suffering,
The delusion regarding the result should not be reversed.
translation: Someone might ask, "If there are no living beings, who gets the result?" That is true, but we only say someone gets it because of our confusion. Still, to calm suffering, we should not get rid of this confusion about the result.

academic_translation:
The pride that is the cause of suffering
Increases through the delusion of a self.
If you say that even that cannot be reversed,
Meditating on selflessness is supreme.
translation: Pride causes suffering. This pride grows from the confusion of a self. Someone might say we cannot get rid of this confusion either. But meditating on no separate self is the best way to stop it.

academic_translation:
The body is not the feet or the calves,
The thighs and the waist are also not the body.
The belly and the back are not the body,
And the chest and the arms are also not the body.
translation: The body is not the feet or the lower legs. The thighs and the waist are not the body either. The belly and the back are not the body. The chest and the arms are not the body.

academic_translation:
The ribs and the hands are also not the body,
The armpits and the shoulders are also not the body.
The internal organs are also not it,
And if the head and the neck are also not the body,
Then what in this is the body?
translation: The ribs and the hands are not the body. The armpits and the shoulders are not the body. The organs inside are not the body either. If the head and the neck are not the body, then what exactly is the body?

academic_translation:
If this body were to abide in all of these
Through its individual portions,
The parts would indeed abide in the parts,
But where would it itself abide?
translation: If this body existed in all of these pieces through its different parts, the parts would just be in the parts. But where would the body itself be?

academic_translation:
If the body in its entirety
Were to abide in the hands and so forth,
However many hands and so forth there are,
There would be that many bodies.
translation: If the whole body existed in the hands and other parts, then however many hands and parts there are, there would be that many bodies.

academic_translation:
If the body does not exist outside or inside,
How does the body exist in the hands and so forth?
If it does not exist as other than the hands and so forth,
How does it exist?
translation: If the body does not exist outside or inside, how does the body exist in the hands and other parts? If it is no different from the hands and other parts, how does it exist?

academic_translation:
Therefore, there is no body; with regard to the hands and so forth,
Due to delusion, the notion of a body arises,
Because of a specific configuration of shape,
Just like the notion of a person with regard to a stump.
translation: Therefore, there is no body. Because of confusion, the idea of a body comes up when looking at the hands and other parts. This happens because of their shape. It is just like mistaking a tree stump for a person.

academic_translation:
As long as the collection of conditions lasts,
The body appears like a person;
Likewise, as long as that is present in the hands and so forth,
For that long, the body appears there.
translation: As long as the gathering of circumstances lasts, the body appears like a person. In the same way, as long as those circumstances are present in the hands and other parts, the body appears to be there.

academic_translation:
Likewise, because it is a collection of fingers,
What would the hand be?
Because that too is a collection of joints,
And the joint, too, by its division into its own parts,
translation: In the same way, what is the hand? It is just a collection of fingers. The finger is also a collection of joints. And a joint can be divided into its own parts.

academic_translation:
Even the part is divided into atoms,
And that atom too, by division into directional parts;
And the directional division too, because it is devoid of parts,
Is like space; therefore, even atoms do not exist.
translation: Even a part is divided into tiny particles. That tiny particle is split into a part in one direction and another. But that split direction has no parts at all. It is just like space. So, even tiny particles do not really exist.

academic_translation:
Thus, to form, which is like a dream,
What discerning person would be attached?
When the body thus does not exist,
Then who is a man and who is a woman?
translation: So, what wise person would hold onto a shape? A shape is just like a dream. When the body does not really exist like this, who is a man? And who is a woman?

academic_translation:
If suffering exists in reality,
Why does it not afflict those who are exceedingly joyful?
If happiness exists, for those tormented by grief and the like,
Why do delicious things and so forth not cause joy?
translation: If suffering is real, why does it not hurt people who are very joyful? If happiness is real, why do delicious foods not bring joy to people who are very sad?

academic_translation:
If you say it is not experienced
Because it is overwhelmed by what is powerful,
How can that which is not of the nature of experience
Be a feeling?
translation: Someone might say you do not have that experience because a stronger force covers it up. But if something is not an experience, how can it be a feeling?

academic_translation:
"Suffering exists in a subtle state."
Has not its coarse state been removed?
If you say, "It is merely a joy distinct from that,"
Then that subtle state too belongs to that.
translation: Someone might say, "Suffering still exists in a faint form." Has its rough state not been removed? If you say, "It is just a different joy," then that faint form also belongs to that joy.

academic_translation:
If, because an opposing condition has arisen,
Suffering does not arise,
Is it not established that what is called feeling
Is nothing but conceptual clinging?
translation: If suffering does not happen because an opposing circumstance comes up, does it not prove something? It shows that what we call a feeling is really just holding on to an idea.

academic_translation:
For this very reason, one should meditate
On this analysis as its antidote;
The meditative concentration arising from the field of investigation
Is the food of the yogi.
translation: For this very reason, we should use meditation on this careful thinking as a remedy. The calm focus that comes from looking closely is the food of the meditation master.

academic_translation:
If there is a gap between the sense faculty and the object,
Where would they meet?
Even if there is no gap, they are just one;
What would meet with what?
translation: If there is a gap between the sense organ and the object, where would they meet? Even if there is no gap, they are just one thing. What would meet with what?

academic_translation:
An atom does not enter an atom;
It lacks space and they are equal.
Without entering, there is no mixing,
And without mixing, there is no meeting.
translation: An atom does not enter another atom. It has no space inside, and they are equal. Without entering, there is no mixing. And without mixing, there is no meeting.

academic_translation:
How could it be logical to say
That what is partless can meet?
If meeting and being partless
Have been seen together, demonstrate it!
translation: How could it make sense to say that something without parts can meet? If you have ever seen meeting and being without parts happen together, show it to me!

academic_translation:
For consciousness, which is without a body,
Meeting is simply not reasonable.
Because a collection, too, lacks an entity,
Just as was analyzed before.
translation: It does not make sense for awareness to meet anything, because it has no body. A gathering is also not a real thing, just as we saw before.

academic_translation:
Thus, if contact does not exist,
From what would feeling arise?
For what purpose is this toil?
What would harm what?
translation: So, if touch does not exist, where would feeling come from? What is the point of all this hard work? What could possibly harm what?

academic_translation:
When there is no feeler at all,
And feeling also does not exist,
Then, seeing this situation,
Why does craving not turn away?
translation: There is no one who feels at all. Feeling does not really exist either. When we see this, why does our wanting not go away?

academic_translation:
Seeing or even touching
Is of a nature like a dream and an illusion;
Because feeling arises simultaneously with the mind,
It is not seen by that mind.
translation: Seeing and touching are just like a dream or an illusion. Feeling happens at the exact same time as the mind. So, the mind cannot see that feeling.

academic_translation:
Even by what arises previously or later,
It is remembered but not experienced.
It does not experience itself,
Nor is it experienced by others.
translation: A mind that comes before or after can only remember it, but cannot experience it. It cannot experience itself. Nothing else can experience it either.

academic_translation:
There is no feeler at all,
Therefore, feeling does not exist in reality.
Thus, how could this collection of selflessness
Be harmed by this?
translation: There is no one who feels at all. Because of this, feeling does not really exist. So how could this harm a collection of parts with no separate self?

academic_translation:
The mind does not abide in the sense faculties,
Nor in forms and so forth, nor in between.
The mind is not inside, nor is it outside,
And it is not found anywhere else.
translation: The mind does not live in a sense organ. It is not in a shape or anything like that, nor anywhere in between. The mind is not inside, and it is not outside. It cannot be found anywhere else either.

academic_translation:
That which is not the body, nor anywhere else,
Not mixed, nor anywhere separate,
Is nothing whatsoever; therefore,
Sentient beings are by nature in nirvāṇa.
translation: It is not the body, and it is not anywhere else. It is not mixed with anything, and it is not separate. It is nothing at all. Because of this, every living being is in freedom from sorrow by nature.

academic_translation:
If consciousness exists before the object of knowledge,
Directed toward what does it arise?
If consciousness and the object of knowledge are simultaneous,
Directed toward what does it arise?
translation: If awareness exists before the thing to know, what is it looking at? If awareness and the thing to know happen at the same time, what is it looking at?
